chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Isa ibn Ayoub from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ismail ibn Abu Al-Hasan from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one upon whom Allah favours with a bounty, so he recognises it in his heart, so he has paid its gratitude.
ai.seo_question: What constitutes the fulfillment of gratitude for Allah's blessings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain to emphasize that true gratitude (shukr) is primarily an internal state of recognition rather than merely external action. This aligns with Shia scholarly tradition, which views the heart's acknowledgment as the foundational prerequisite for the physical and verbal expressions of thankfulness. It underscores the spiritual depth of worship, where inner conviction validates outward deeds.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Isa Bin Ayoub, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ismail, Bin Abu Al hassan, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one upon whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours with a Bounty, so he recognises it in his heart, so he has paid its gratitude’.
en.sarwar: 15. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from ‘Isa ibn Ayyub from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Isma’il ibn abu al-Hassan from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whoever receives a favor from Allah and acknowledges it in his heart, in so doing he has expressed his thankfuness for it also.”’
